sections.overview: Manduca florestan is a New World hawkmoth ranging from the southwestern United States southward.
sections.identification: Adults have grey-brown forewings with pale patches and dark marks.
sections.habitat: It reaches Mexico, Central America and South America; habitat detail is sparse.
sections.diet: Caterpillars use several woody plant families, including Bignoniaceae, Boraginaceae and Verbenaceae; adults feed on flower nectar.
sections.behavior: The caterpillar bears the tail horn typical of many sphinxes.
sections.reproduction: A pupa precedes adult emergence; timing across its range is unclear.
sections.ecology: Argentine records list hosts from three plant families. By comparison, the Costa Rican inventory of Manduca albiplaga larvae found them on Annonaceae; see that profile for details.
sections.conservation: Sources reviewed give no global population trend for this moth.
